newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sun sees $100 mln investment in Pacific Rim.
newsitem.headline: Sun sees $100 mln investment in Pacific Rim.

text.p: U.S.-based Sun Microsystems Inc is likely to increase its investment in the Pacific Rim to US$100 million over the next few years, chairman and chief executive officer Scott McNealy said on Monday.

"We will continue to ramp up our investment and I would imagine over the next few years, our investment both direct and indirect, will be in the $100 million kind of range in the Pacific Rim," McNealy said in Singapore.
McNealy was in Singapore to receive a business headquarters status award for Sun from the Economic Development Board.
To date, Sun has invested about $50 million in the region.
McNealy said the incremental investment would be mostly for "knowledge transfer" and in advertising and marketing.
Sun is setting up "competency centres and factories" to promote programming in its Java language.
Java is a computer language developed by Sun that enables software to run on different computer systems.
In a presentation to reporters, McNealy presented the case for computing called the "fat server, big pipes, thin clients" model.
This model uses the concept of simple-to-use devices like network computers that tap into networks for all kinds of resources, including the operating system and applications.
McNealy said all kinds of devices from smart cards, watches, set-top boxes to mainframes can be programmed with Java for easy use and greater security than Microsoft-Intel systems.
"We want to make computing as easy as working a telephone, hair dryer or a faucet," he said.
McNealy said Sun was slightly slow in localising Java for different countries but was working hard on it.
McNealy said he saw the Java smart card becoming available this year.
But he conceded that the PC based on the Microsoft-Intel concept would be around for a long time.
